name: Development Work Plan
one_liner: The container of three plans: what to build, when, and how.
purpose: The Development Work Plan gathers the information needed to manage the development aspect of the project — a container of different perspectives on what needs to be done and how the development goals will be achieved. It includes the Work Items List, the corresponding Release Plan and the supporting Iteration Plans, and these three elements let the A-PCT set and manage the expectations of the rest of the project organisation. It is a living artefact, kept current with new detail, progress and changing business priorities, and it becomes part of the Project Work Plan.

fields.what: All items to be addressed in the IT-domain aspect — user stories, enabler stories, bugs — prioritised and estimated.
fields.pollux: Curie's list: 96 open items at the RfE gate, every one estimated in points and MoSCoW-ranked.

fields.what: The release-level schedule. Its focus is primarily on what needs to be done and when.
fields.pollux: Four releases: 29 Mar, 28 Jun, 27 Sep and 20 Dec 2029.

fields.what: The iteration-level schedule. Its focus is on how the work will be done by the A-PCT.
fields.pollux: One plan per two-week iteration; iteration 1 opened 08 Jan 2029.

fields.what: Release Plan answers what and when; Iteration Plan answers how. The examinable distinction between the two schedules.
fields.pollux: Release 2 says 'reconciliation panel by 28 Jun'; iteration 9 says how the panel gets built.

fields.what: Viewed as a container of different perspectives on what needs to be done and how the goals will be achieved.
fields.pollux: POLLUX keeps no Work Plan document — the three views are queries over one tool.

fields.what: The three elements together let the A-PCT set and manage the expectations of the rest of the project organisation.
fields.pollux: Gantt's 'agile means no schedule' objection answered by showing all three levels at once.

fields.what: The Development Work Plan becomes part of the Project Work Plan, and must align with it.
fields.pollux: Release dates appear unchanged in the POLLUX Project Work Plan and the Charter milestones.

fields.what: Aligned with the important project milestones as defined by the Project Manager and the whole Project Core Team.
fields.pollux: Transition into service 31 Jan 2030 constrains Release 4 to 20 Dec 2029.

fields.what: Kept current by incorporating new information, detail and work progress status as they become available.
fields.pollux: Re-baselined after every Release Planning; v2.0 dated 27 Nov 2028, v6.2 during Release 3.

fields.what: Updated as often as necessary to capture changing business priorities — changes in the WIL or in the Release Plan's contents.
fields.pollux: Scenario overlay moved from Release 4 to Release 3 after Risk's Q2 2029 request.

fields.what: All work items need to be prioritised and estimated at some point, because the WIL is the main driver of the project.
fields.pollux: Relative estimates in points from planning poker; absolute hours only for iteration tasks.

fields.what: TeCo collects data on all activities defining the Development Work Plan in general, and the Release Plan in particular.
fields.pollux: Lovelace runs Release Planning and keeps the release-level view current.

fields.what: Provides technical advice and constraints per iteration, and helps the PrOw prioritise the WIL and organise the release plans.
fields.pollux: Einstein negotiates enabler share per release: never zero, never three iterations in a row.

fields.what: Actively support the whole plan and play a critical role in the definition of the Iteration Plans.
fields.pollux: Lamarr, Babbage and Eiffel size the iteration and decide task breakdown themselves.

fields.what: As accountable, must know how the A-PCT plans to deliver and how that aligns with overall project milestones.
fields.pollux: You review the plan at each release boundary and carry it into the Project Work Plan.

fields.what: Can be documented in varied formats and media — MS Office documentation or tools such as JIRA or Rational Team Concert.
fields.who: TeCo · tailoring in the Development Handbook
fields.pollux: One tool holds WIL, releases and iterations; exports feed the Project Work Plan.

traps: Development Work Plan becomes part of the Project Work Plan — it does not replace it.
It is three things: Work Items List, Release Plan, Iteration Plan.
TeCo is Responsible overall, but the PrOw is Responsible for the WIL.
Release Plan = what and when; Iteration Plan = how. Do not swap them.
Created in Planning, updated in Executing — never in Initiating.
